title: Predictive Request Prioritization and Soft-Quota Patterns
author: Priya Nair
content:
Summary
-------
This doc describes a set of platform patterns we use to keep tenant-facing LLM inference services within SLOs while optimizing for cost and fairness: predictive request scoring, soft-quotas (adaptive throttling), and runtime hedging / safety-net fallbacks. It covers rationale, scoring algorithm, configuration knobs, dashboards and alerting, rollout steps, and an operator runbook for common failure modes.

Why this exists
----------------
- We observed large tails of latency and token-cost variability driven by a small fraction of requests and tenants.
- Hard throttles create poor customer experience and billing surprises.
- A combined approach (predictive prioritization + soft quotas + hedging) lets us preserve premium SLOs while providing graceful degradation for lower-priority work.

Goals and SLO implications
-------------------------
- Preserve 99th-percentile latency SLO for premium routes: target p99 <= 600ms for short-chat requests.
- Keep cost-per-1k-token variance within 20% month-over-month for top 80% of traffic.
- Minimize hard rejections: target <0.5% 429s for production tenants.

Definitions
-----------
- Request score: a numeric priority computed at ingress (0..100). Higher is higher priority.
- Soft-quota: a sliding allocation window (tokens/sec or requests/minute) enforced with probabilistic throttling rather than deterministic rejections.
- Hedging: duplicate or fast-fallback requests sent to a cheaper model or cached result to avoid tail latency at the cost of additional resource use.

Design overview
---------------
1) Ingress scoring pipeline: lightweight scoring executed in the edge proxy (envoy filter or edge lambda) that attaches a score header to the request.
   - Inputs: tenant tier, route, recent error/latency indicators from tracing, request length estimate (tokens), client-provided priority hints (if allowed).
   - Output: X-Redwood-Req-Score header (integer 0..100).
2) Soft-quota enforcement in the request router: the router maintains per-tenant sliding windows and applies a probabilistic allow/deny decision based on the score and current usage.
3) Hedging and fallback: when a request is predicted to miss the latency SLO, we optionally issue a parallel request to a cached or lower-cost path and accept the first acceptable answer.

Scoring algorithm (reference)
----------------------------
- Base score by tier: premium=80, standard=50, free=20.
- Route multiplier: chat=1.0, embeddings=0.9, batch-rerank=0.7.
- Recent tail factor: add up to +15 if tenant has low recent p99 violations; subtract up to -30 if tenant caused >1% p99 errors in last 10m.
- Token-length penalty: score -= min(20, floor(tokens_estimate/200) * 5).
- Client-priority hint: add up to +10 when signed and allowed by policy.
- Final: clamp to 0..100 and attach as header.

Pseudo-code
-----------
```
function compute_score(tenant, route, tokens_estimate, hint):
  s = base_by_tier(tenant.tier)                       # 20/50/80
  s = s * route_multiplier(route)
  s += recent_tail_adjustment(tenant)                 # -30..+15
  s -= token_length_penalty(tokens_estimate)
  if is_valid_hint(hint): s += hint_value(hint)
  return clamp(round(s), 0, 100)
```

Soft-quota policy model
-----------------------
We implement a token-based soft quota per-tenant with the following characteristics:
- Sliding window of 60s for short-term burst control and 1-hour exponential moving average for fair-share.
- Allow probability = sigmoid( alpha * (score_normalized - usage_ratio) + bias )
  - usage_ratio = current_tokens_window / quota_limit
  - alpha, bias tuned per-beta tenants.
- Hard reject threshold only when usage_ratio > 3x quota_limit and score < 10.

Configuration table (example keys and recommended defaults)
----------------------------------------------------------
| key | description | recommended default | notes |
|----|-------------|--------------------|-------|
| quota.tokens_per_min | short-term token budget | 200000 | per-tenant baseline for standard tier |
| quota.tokens_hour_ema | long-term smoothing | 6e6 | used for fair-share |
| scoring.alpha | soft-quota sigmoid steepness | 75 | higher => more binary decisions |
| scoring.bias | soft-quota bias term | 0.05 | small positive to favor requests |
| hedging.enabled | global hedging toggle | true | must be off for restricted customers |
| hedging.primary_timeout_ms | time to wait before firing hedge | 250 | tuned to p95/p99 gap |
| fallback.model_set | ordered list of fallback model ids | ["redwood-small-v1","redwood-quantized-1"] | cheaper, lower-quality models |

Dashboard and metrics
---------------------
Instrument the following at per-tenant and route granularity:
- request.score.histogram (0..100 buckets)
- requests.allowed_by_soft_quota.count, requests.soft_rejected.count
- tokens.windowed.sum, tokens.hour_ema.value
- hedged_requests.count, hedged_requests.win_ratio
- tail_latency.p95, p99 by route and tier

Recommended dashboard panels:
- Priority distribution heatmap (score vs route)
- Soft-quota allowance rate over time (per top-50 tenants)
- Hedge efficacy: fraction of time hedged request returned first and improved latency
- Cost impact: incremental tokens from hedging vs avoided p99 incidents

Alerting rules (examples)
------------------------
1) Elevated soft_rejected rate: if requests.soft_rejected.count / requests.total > 1% over 10m for premium tier => P1 alert to SRE team.
2) Unexpected hedging cost: hedged_tokens.delta > 300% baseline in 30m => P2 to platform-cost.
3) Tenant p99 regression: p99.latency increase > 30% and 50ms absolute over baseline => P1 and trigger canary rollback.

Rollout plan
------------
1. Lab stage (dev): deploy scoring to canary edge and simulate tenant traces using recorded production traffic (replay) with scoring off for decisioning.
2. Beta tenants (2–5 customers): enable scoring in passive mode (attach header only) and run dashboards for 2 weeks. Collect score distribution and false-positive analysis.
3. Soft enforcement for non-critical tenants: enable soft-quotas for 10% of standard and free tenants, monitor allow rate and p99s for premium.
4. Gradual rollout to all tenants with automated rollback conditions baked into canary orchestration.

Operational runbook (common scenarios)
-------------------------------------
- Symptom: sudden spike in soft_rejected for premium tenants.
  1) Check recent deployment diff to edge scoring pipeline.
  2) Inspect score distribution and recent_tail_adjustment to see if a scoring regression penalized tenants.
  3) If scoring bug suspected, flip scoring to passive mode and scale up short-term quota for affected tenants.
  4) Post-incident: root cause, update tests in scoring unit tests.

- Symptom: hedging costs blow up without latency improvement.
  1) Disable hedging globally (feature flag) for 5 minutes, observe dropped cost.
  2) Review hedging.primary_timeout_ms and p95/p99 gap telemetry; tune timeout upward if hedges fire too aggressively.
  3) Re-enable hedging with reduced tenant set.

Failure modes and mitigations
---------------------------
- Scoring bias drift: periodic chaos test where we inject synthetic high-scoring low-priority traffic and verify fairness.
- Exploitable client hints: require signed client hints for any priority uplift; unauthenticated hints are ignored.
- Time-of-day flash: adjust short-term quota to be more permissive during predictable nightly batch windows.

Testing and validation checklist
-------------------------------
1) Unit tests for compute_score with corner cases (long tokens, negative tail adjustments).
2) End-to-end replay test against staging with canary traffic generator; assert p99 and cost delta under thresholds.
3) Integration test for hedging to ensure dedupe and idempotency of downstream side-effects.

Ownership and next steps
------------------------
- Product owner: Priya Nair (platform-scheduling).
- SRE contact: Ethan Liu.
- Follow-ups: run a two-week fairness analysis after full rollout; evaluate moving to ML-based scoring if static heuristics fail to meet fairness targets.

Appendix A — Example envoy filter config snippet
------------------------------------------------
```
filters:
- name: envoy.filters.http.lua
  typed_config:
    "@type": type.googleapis.com/envoy.extensions.filters.http.lua.v3.Lua
    inline_code: |
      function envoy_on_request(request_handle)
        local tenant = request_handle:headers():get("x-tenant-id") or "unknown"
        local tier = lookup_tier(tenant)
        local tokens_est = estimate_tokens(request_handle:body())
        local score = compute_score_local(tier, request_handle:headers()[":path"], tokens_est)
        request_handle:headers():add("x-redwood-req-score", tostring(score))
      end
```

Appendix B — Example dashboard query (Prometheus style)
-----------------------------------------------------
- soft_allow_rate = sum(rate(requests_allowed_by_soft_quota_count[5m])) / sum(rate(requests_total[5m]))

Lessons learned (retrospective notes)
------------------------------------
- Start passive: attaching metadata without enforcement surfaced many edge cases and reduced rollback risk.
- Simpler heuristics first: static heuristics covered many immediate fairness issues; ML can be incremental.
- Observability first: we needed a heatmap (score vs tenant) to find scoring cliff edges early.
